picks.name: Fūunji (風雲児)
picks.address: Yoyogi 2-14-3, Shibuya (2 min from Shinjuku South Exit)
picks.verdict: The single most recommended ramen spot in Shinjuku across all of Reddit — and it's tsukemen.
picks.whatToOrder: Tsukemen (dipping noodles) with the rich fish + pork broth. Get the large size — it's the same price. Add ajitama (seasoned egg).

picks.name: Ramen Nagi Golden Gai (凪)
picks.verdict: 24-hour niboshi ramen in the heart of Golden Gai — the most atmospheric bowl in Shinjuku.
picks.whatToOrder: The special bowl (tokumori) from the vending machine. Niboshi (dried sardine) broth is thick and intensely savory — unlike anything you'll find back home.

picks.name: Ramen Tatsunoya (龍の家)
picks.verdict: Highest-rated ramen in Shinjuku at 4.4★ — Kurume-style tonkotsu done to perfection.
picks.whatToOrder: Koku (rich) tonkotsu with extra chashu. The broth is milky-white and deeply porky without being heavy. Add a nitamago (stewed egg).

picks.name: Tsukemen Gonokami Seisakusho (五ノ神製作所)
picks.verdict: The shrimp tsukemen that Reddit can't stop recommending — thick, rich, and totally unique.
picks.whatToOrder: Ebi (shrimp) tsukemen with the pesto topping — trust Reddit on this one. The broth is thick, creamy, and intensely shrimpy.

picks.name: Soushi Menya Musashi (麺屋武蔵)
picks.verdict: The legendary Musashi chain's flagship — 14 stores in Tokyo, each with a completely different menu.
picks.whatToOrder: Gyokai (seafood) tsukemen — their signature. The dipping broth is a thick blend of chicken, pork, and bonito that hits every umami note.

picks.name: Ramen Hayashida (林田)
picks.verdict: One of the best ramen shops in all of Tokyo — not just Shinjuku. 14 branches and counting.
picks.whatToOrder: Special shoyu ramen with all toppings. The broth is a clear, deep golden shoyu that's deceptively complex. Add the ajitama.

picks.name: Ramen Takahashi (高はし)
picks.verdict: Kabukichō's go-to for late-night ramen — open until 2 AM on weekends.
picks.whatToOrder: Their signature shoyu ramen — simple, clean, satisfying. Perfect for a 1 AM refuel after Golden Gai.

picks.name: Menya Kaijin (麺屋海神)
picks.verdict: A lighter, seafood-forward option that's perfect if you're tired of heavy tonkotsu.
picks.whatToOrder: Asa-ramen (morning ramen) — their signature light seafood shio with whole baby fish floating in the bowl. Surprisingly elegant for ramen.

picks.name: Konjiki Hototogisu (金色不如帰)
picks.verdict: Michelin Bib Gourmand-level hamaguri (clam) shio ramen — the connoisseur's pick.
picks.whatToOrder: Hamaguri (clam) shio soba — their signature. The broth is ethereal — light, golden, with subtle truffle oil. A different dimension of ramen.

picks.name: Menya Sho (麺屋翔)
picks.verdict: Homey chicken ramen with the best chashu slices multiple Redditors have ever had.
picks.whatToOrder: Tokusei (special) chicken shio ramen with extra chashu. The broth is clean and golden, the chashu is melt-in-your-mouth tender.

picks.name: Ebisoba Ichigen (えびそば一幻)
picks.verdict: Hokkaido's famous shrimp ramen chain, brought to Shinjuku — pink-hued broth that's unmistakable.
picks.whatToOrder: Ebisoba miso (shrimp miso ramen) with the sono-mama (pure shrimp) broth option. The pink-hued, intensely shrimpy soup is nothing like standard ramen.

picks.name: Ramen Hōsenka (鳳仙花)
picks.verdict: Creamy chicken paitan that multiple locals call the best in the ward.
picks.whatToOrder: Tokusei tori paitan ramen — the rich chicken broth is opaque white and incredibly creamy. Add the ajitama and extra noodles (kaedama).

picks.name: Ramen Afro Beats
picks.verdict: The newcomer sensation — 4.4★ and Reddit's 'top 3 ramen in all of Japan' calls.
picks.whatToOrder: Tokusei tori paitan with all toppings. The chicken broth is impossibly rich and silky — more like a French bisque than typical ramen.
